about: What this member said on the floor, from the Congressional Record: their own words only, and of those the sentences that name an alignment question's phrases or make a commitment. Written by npm run record:collect (scripts/collect-record.mjs).
name: Brad Sherman

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: COMMON CENTS ACT
statements.title: COMMON CENTS ACT
sentences: Unfortunately, the decision to stop minting pennies ignored the authority of Congress in regulating currency and overseeing a major transition away from producing pennies.
This will be a boon to our transit agencies, vending machines, and others when people use a dollar coin.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 10167, the Common Cents Act, sponsored by Representative McClain.
Now, we will be rounding to the nearest nickel instead of rounding to the nearest penny.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GUARDING UNPROTECTED AGING RETIREES FROM DECEPTION ACT OF 2026
statements.title: GUARDING UNPROTECTED AGING RETIREES FROM DECEPTION ACT OF 2026
sentences: The GUARD Act would allow State, local, and Tribal law enforcement agencies to tap into certain Federal grant programs to support investigations into senior fraud, romance scams, and general financial fraud.
The bill would also permit Federal law enforcement to assist State and local law enforcement with tracing tools for blockchain technology.

This bill is particularly important because blockchain technology, cryptocurrency, is so often used in scams, and it is the Federal Government that has the best chance--and it is only a chance--of using technology to defeat the scams and to hold those responsible accountable.

Mr. Speaker, the GUARD Act allows State, local, and Tribal law enforcement agencies to use certain Federal grant programs to investigate senior financial fraud, romance schemes, and general financial fraud.
The first is that crypto has facilitated frauds and scams, and it is necessary that we give law enforcement the tools to react to that.
I rise in support of H.R. 2978, the GUARD Act, sponsored by Representatives Nunn and Gottheimer.
I support this bill, but I must express a significant concern of the Democratic Caucus that should be addressed.
There are two points that I made in my earlier statement that I will reiterate.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FOSTERING THE USE OF TECHNOLOGY TO UPHOLD REGULATORY EFFECTIVENESS IN SUPERVISION ACT
statements.title: FOSTERING THE USE OF TECHNOLOGY TO UPHOLD REGULATORY EFFECTIVENESS IN SUPERVISION ACT
sentences: For example, on July 23, 2025, an executive order directed agencies not to procure AI models that contain AI outputs driven by ideologies like diversity, equality, and inclusion.
I rise in support of H.R. 8278, the Fostering the Use of Technology to Uphold Regulatory Effectiveness in Supervision Act, as amended, authored by Representative Stutzman.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: WHISTLEBLOWER PROTECTION ACT OF 2025
statements.title: WHISTLEBLOWER PROTECTION ACT OF 2025
sentences: The two best tools for dealing with waste, fraud, and abuse are inspectors general, full-time independent investigators there to stop waste, fraud, and abuse, and whistleblowers, ordinary government workers who come forward to tell us what is going on.
This bill strengthens the whistleblower part of that equation, but we have to reflect on the fact that this President has gutted the first part, the inspectors general.
The whistleblower part of oversight only works when people can speak up without fear of retaliation, and that is why whistleblower protections are so important.
Whistleblowers are now the last line of defense against these harmful decisions made behind closed doors, and Congress needs to send a clear message: If you expose wrongdoing, you will be protected.
Whistleblowers are how we catch waste, fraud, and abuse before they spiral.
It strengthens whistleblower protections and makes them consistent across HUD contractors without gaps and without guesswork.
We also need whistleblower protection.
This bill will provide additional protection for whistleblowers.
Protecting whistleblowers is not a partisan issue.
For that reason, I support H.R. 4646.
For that reason, I urge my colleagues to support H.R. 4646.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REBUILDING USAID
statements.title: REBUILDING USAID
sentences: Mr. Speaker, foreign aid has been a political whipping boy in this country for decades.
The American people believe, if you poll them, that we spend 25 percent of our Nation's budget on foreign aid and they want it reduced to 10 percent.
But let's focus on public health because what USAID does more than anything else is fight malaria, Ebola, tuberculosis, and HIV-AIDS.
Mr. Speaker, I thank 120 Members of the House who joined with my letter urging the Appropriations Committee to fully fund foreign aid.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: NATIONAL SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF STATE, AND RELATED PROGRAMS APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2027
statements.title: NATIONAL SECURITY, DEPARTMENT OF STATE, AND RELATED PROGRAMS APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2027
sentences: That is as bad an idea as Donald Trump's repudiation of the JCPOA, the deal with Iran that limited its nuclear program.
This $3.3 billion provides the AMRAAM system that defends Israeli apartment buildings and houses from incoming missiles that have as one purpose: to kill as many Israeli civilians as possible.
How are we going to influence the people of Israel and the government of Israel?

Republican leadership has brought it to the floor--not for the purpose of having it become law, but for the purpose of driving a wedge through the middle of the Democratic Party, for the purpose of facilitating Republican advertisements that will put our party on the side of those who are screaming death to America and death to Israel, and to put our party on the side of those who say that Israel has no right to exist.
Now that does not mean that there will not be future reductions in our aid to Israel.

That does not mean that we will not try to change Israeli policy, but this amendment goes as far as it possibly can to put us on the side not of those who would shoot down the missiles that are aimed at civilian neighborhoods in Israel but on those who are cheering those missiles.
It says $3.3 billion, but that is about an 80th of the aid that we have provided Ukraine and that we should have provided Ukraine.
This is not an attempt to divert a large portion of our money from Israel.
This is an attack on the Israeli people.
We will not fund the AMRAAM system that is provided for in a memorandum of understanding signed by President Obama.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HOUSING FOR THE 21ST CENTURY ACT
statements.title: HOUSING FOR THE 21ST CENTURY ACT
sentences: There is nothing more shameful for our country than a homeless disabled veteran.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: SHARAREH MOGHADDAM'S DETENTION
statements.title: SHARAREH MOGHADDAM'S DETENTION
sentences: A habeas corpus petition challenging her detention is currently pending before a judge, and her family is simply asking for a fair and timely decision.
I have spent 30 years fighting to make sure that Iran never has a nuclear weapon.
He has said in the past that he wants the same deal as Iran got.
Well, I don't think he wants that deal now because Iran is not looking all that good.

Mr. Speaker, I have always felt that any nuclear cooperation agreements, particularly in the Middle East, should meet the highest level of safeguards so that, in an effort to allow for the creation of nuclear power, we don't see a clandestine effort to develop a nuclear weapon.
These are safeguards fully consistent with the efficient and economic production of nuclear power.
It was 1978, and the most powerful Middle East monarch was the Shah of Iran, a good friend of the United States.

Right now, only certain countries have nuclear weapons: the five that won World War II; India and Pakistan that face off against each other; and North Korea, a pariah state that does face genuine challenges to its security.
No one is calling for the abolition of Saudi Arabia, as they call for the abolition of Israel.

Now, at that time, I put forward the idea that there was a race between those that would create computer intelligence, self-aware perhaps, and massively exceeding human intelligence, and the possibility--not talked about much now, but given the CRISPR technology, still a possibility--that the genetic engineers would create a 1,000-pound mammal with a 50-pound brain able to beat my daughter on the law school admissions test.
Right now, the artificial intelligence engineers are way ahead.

We are spending as a species nothing to make sure that this artificial intelligence is not self-aware, self- motivated, has a survival instinct, has ambitions of its own, and has a desire to affect the world for its own reasons.
The title tells you everything: ``If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies.'' It starts with the idea that artificial intelligence will soon exceed human intelligence.
The other possibility is that artificial intelligence has no desires whatsoever.
There is no evidence yet that AI or any artificial intelligence has a survival instinct.

I have put forward a bill to establish an AI Research and Threat Assessment Act, so that we actually try, if we are going to have the big box with incredible artificial intelligence in it, that we put on top a small box that we need to develop to monitor and prevent self- awareness, ambition, survival instinct, a desire to affect the world, and a desire to have its own desires.
But the fact is that whether the artificial intelligence that ends the human species comes from Shanghai or the Silicon Valley will matter little, really not at all.
We will use genetic engineering to prevent this, and we will use AI, assuming we are still running the planet, to develop the genetic engineering.

So, we are fighting over all these ideas, all the problems of today, all of the issues, all of the fact that the most important thing for us to do is to build a subway through the Sepulveda Pass, and it is.
But I expect that subway to last well more than 100 years.
We need to look first at artificial intelligence.
We need to make sure that artificial intelligence is monitored for and that we prevent ambition, survival instinct, self-direction.
I will not give up, and the San Fernando Valley will not give up until you come home.
I will be introducing the No Nuclear Weapons for Saudi Arabia Act.
I believe we are going to do that tomorrow.
Mr. Speaker, I will deal with a third issue, an issue I first addressed on this floor in the year 2020.
We are going to be living in a science fiction movie.
I am not quite so sure that we will get there in just a few years.
First, we will repair humans using our DNA technology.
Once we make sure that everybody has good intelligence, we will go to enhanced intelligence.
Then we will go from the repaired human to the enhanced human, to the trans-human, or we may not even start with human DNA.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MIRACLE ON ICE CONGRESSIONAL GOLD MEDAL ACT
statements.title: MIRACLE ON ICE CONGRESSIONAL GOLD MEDAL ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of concurring in the Senate amendment and passing H.R. 452, the Miracle on Ice Congressional Gold Medal Act, sponsored by our friend, Pete Stauber.
We will see that at 10:10 eastern time, when the Dodgers defeat the Philadelphia Phillies tonight.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DIGITAL ASSET MARKET CLARITY ACT OF 2025
statements.title: DIGITAL ASSET MARKET CLARITY ACT OF 2025
sentences: This bill is an attack on working families, which is why the AFL-CIO says no, and they are scoring it.
This bill prohibits Congress Members from sponsoring cryptocurrencies because of the obvious corruption and conflict of interest, but it allows the President to create electronic Monopoly money.
Abu Dhabi is buying $2 billion of Trump stablecoin while the Chinese interests behind TikTok are buying $300 million worth of Trump coin, and that is just what we know about.
There is a lot we don't know about because cryptocurrency literally means hidden money.
Congress won't stop him because crypto spends more in super-PAC than any other industry by far, five times more than the combination of Big Oil and Big Pharma.
It allows for the purchase of bitcoin and Trump coin, and Trump has announced that he is going to do just that with our tax dollars going into his crypto.
Finally, this creates the perfect financial tool for drug dealers and for tax evaders because every time a billionaire cheats on his taxes, a member of the Freedom Caucus earns his wings.
I will not be offering it because in the absence of the other amendments, it is really not useful.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: GUIDING AND ESTABLISHING NATIONAL INNOVATION FOR U.S. STABLECOINS ACT
statements.title: GUIDING AND ESTABLISHING NATIONAL INNOVATION FOR U.S. STABLECOINS ACT
sentences: He is the genius behind this GENIUS Act, and one can only hope that he is able to watch C-SPAN on a black-and-white television set in his prison cell.
You don't have to be a genius to know that this bill is an attack on working families.
Who wants to forgo a 4 percent rate of return and get a zero percent return in stablecoin?
Those who are desperate for what cryptocurrency offers.
Cryptocurrency literally means hidden money, and these stablecoins are exempt from the anti-money laundering provisions.
Mixers are devices whose sole purpose is to defeat even top law enforcement efforts pursuant to a warrant, and under this bill mixers will be used to defeat law enforcement.
Page 43 of this bill contains a provision maintaining the eligibility of stablecoins for bailouts under a facility created under section 13(3) of the Federal Reserve Act.
Now, Jerome Powell won't bail out stablecoin, but the next guy will.
Stablecoin marketers are going to tell investors that if they ever have a problem they are going to get bailed out.
After all, crypto has all the power in Congress because it is the number one source of super- PAC independent expenditures.
Last year, crypto did more super-PAC expenditures than Big Oil and Big Pharma times five.
Even Richard Nixon never thought of printing up baskets of Monopoly money and selling them for cash.
Abu Dhabi has announced they are investing $2 billion in Trump stablecoin, $2 billion in Trump's hands where he has to pay nothing, zero percent, on the loan.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ANTI-CBDC SURVEILLANCE STATE ACT
statements.title: ANTI-CBDC SURVEILLANCE STATE ACT
sentences: The largest super-PAC expenditures in history occurred last year.
If you combine all of the expenditures from Big Oil plus Big Pharma, put them together, and multiply by five, you still don't have what the crypto industry did last year.

Now, I think Americans will always have banks, credit cards, debit cards, Zelle, Venmo, cash, money market funds, and pursuant to the bill that it looks like we are going to pass today, they will have stablecoin, a privacy device specifically designed for criminals and tax evaders.
Then they will have mixers to make it impossible for even the most advanced law enforcement, even with a warrant, to find out what is happening.
You are not allowed to have the currency provided for in the U.S. Constitution.
They say the Chinese Communist Party can have a digital yuan, the bitcoin bros can have a digital currency, but America is limited to 1776 technology.

It will provide an avenue for foreign interests to provide hidden money--``cryptocurrency'' literally means hidden money--into Trump's personal pocket, and it is designed to allow taxpayer money to be used to buy bitcoin and Trump coin.
It says that you can have freedom to have a digital currency only if you do it in a way that it enriches the crypto bros.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AFL-CIO SCORING CRYPTO BILLS
statements.title: AFL-CIO SCORING CRYPTO BILLS
sentences: The AFL-CIO has sent a letter to every Member, saying that these bills are an attack on working families and that they will score your vote on these issues, and to vote ``no'' on both bills.
It means they can print their electronic monopoly money.
China is buying $300 million, and Abu Dhabi has agreed to buy $2 billion of Trump coin or Trump stablecoin.
It allows for the purchase with your U.S. tax dollars of Bitcoin or Trump coin.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 4016, DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3633, DIGITAL ASSET MARKET CLARITY ACT
statements.title: PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 4016, DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE APPROPRIATIONS ACT, 2026; PROVIDING FOR CONSIDERATION OF H.R. 3633, DIGITAL ASSET MARKET CLARITY ACT OF 2025; PROVIDING FOR...
sentences: If you vote against this rule, you are voting to allow him to buy bitcoin or Trump coin with taxpayer money.
That second amendment, also prohibited by this rule, says that taxpayer money will not be used to bail out stablecoin or other crypto assets.
They gave us just a patina of regulation, and if there is ever a problem with your crypto assets, we will get you bailed out.
It tells us that we are supposed to be for innovation and blockchain.
Then it calls for the prohibition of the Fed having blockchain or any electronic use of the U.S. dollar.

The Constitution says currency is what the U.S. Congress should control, but this bill will say that the dollar must use George Washington technology while China can have a digital yuan and the crypto bros can have hidden digital money.
Mr. Speaker, don't tell us we can't release the Epstein files because you hate Joe Biden or because you hate leftists.
People on the right, people in the center, and everyone who wants to protect girls in America says to release the Epstein files now.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TAIWAN NON-DISCRIMINATION ACT OF 2025
statements.title: TAIWAN NON-DISCRIMINATION ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 910, the Taiwan Non- Discrimination Act of 2025, sponsored by Representative Kim from California and cosponsored by Representative Green of Texas.

Congress should support this bill, and I urge my Republican colleagues not only to urge that Donald Trump carry this bill out but also support the people of Taiwan and support the role of the IMF as we go forward.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: AGRICULTURAL RISK REVIEW ACT OF 2025
statements.title: AGRICULTURAL RISK REVIEW ACT OF 2025
sentences: Recognizing the importance of safe food and of national security involving agriculture, H.R. 1713 also requires CFIUS to determine whether a national security review is necessary upon notification from the Secretary of Agriculture that an agricultural land transaction could somehow affect national security.
When they buy farmland, they can't take the land back to China, and they can't take the food back to China unless we decide to let them.
I don't think that the purchase of farmland poses the risks that are being overblown.

Finally, I think the withdrawal of the United States from the World Health Organization and illegally ending American food programs also exposes the entire world and ultimately the United States to substantial risks.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 1713, the Agricultural Risk Review Act of 2025, sponsored by Representative Lucas.
I urge my Republican colleagues also to work to protect SNAP, the USDA, and our efforts at global health.

I urge my Republican colleagues not only to support this bill but to support the activities of the Department of Agriculture, including SNAP, food inspections, and other efforts designed to make sure that our food supply is safe, available, and secure.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HELPING ANGELS LEAD OUR STARTUPS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: HELPING ANGELS LEAD OUR STARTUPS ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 3352, the Helping Angels Lead Our Startups Act, or HALOS Act of 2025, sponsored by the gentleman from New York (Mr. Lawler).
Mr. Speaker, I urge all Members to support H.R. 3352, the Helping Angels Lead Our Startups Act, or HALOS Act, sponsored by Mr. Lawler.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ACCESS TO SMALL BUSINESS INVESTOR CAPITAL ACT
statements.title: ACCESS TO SMALL BUSINESS INVESTOR CAPITAL ACT
sentences: BDCs are often the first institutional investors to step in.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FAIR INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR PROFESSIONAL EXPERTS ACT
statements.title: FAIR INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES FOR PROFESSIONAL EXPERTS ACT
sentences: There are not the same legal protections for investors either, nor is there the same ability of the SEC or the State securities regulators to police these markets.
Those were definitions applicable in 1983 that may not have defined those with the requisite knowledge, but at least defined those who were high-income, high-net worth individuals.
Back then, roughly 2 percent of all Americans were considered accredited investors.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 3394, the Fair Investment Opportunities for Professional Experts Act, offered by my friend and Financial Services Committee chair, French Hill.

At the same time, I will point out that our definition of ``accredited investor'' was, I think, wrongfully decided that we should just focus on whoever is rich, then defined people as rich based on 1983 numbers.
I rise in support of this bill.
Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of Chairman Hill's bill, H.R. 3394.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ENCOURAGING LOCAL EMERGING VENTURES AND ECONOMIC GROWTH ACT OF 2025
statements.title: ENCOURAGING LOCAL EMERGING VENTURES AND ECONOMIC GROWTH ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 3301, the ELEVATE Act of 2025, sponsored by the gentlewoman from Iowa (Mr. Nunn).

I urge my colleagues to support the ELEVATE Act of 2025, which would streamline accounting disclosure requirements and auditing requirements for emerging growth companies, also known as EGCs, so those EGCs only need to provide 2 years of audited financial statements across the board.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ENCOURAGING PUBLIC OFFERINGS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: ENCOURAGING PUBLIC OFFERINGS ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mrs. Wagner's bill also codifies a 2019 SEC rulemaking that allows any issuer to test the waters before going public, which would allow any issuer to gauge institutional investor interest in their offering without first needing to file a registration statement with the SEC.

I urge my colleagues to vote ``yes'' on H.R. 3381, the Encouraging Public Offerings Act of 2025 sponsored by the chair of our subcommittee, the gentlewoman from Missouri (Mrs. Wagner), which would allow issuers to take advantage of confidential draft registration statements that are currently available only to EGCs.
It also makes it easier for companies to have access to capital by giving them the ability to gauge interest from institutional investors without added regulatory requirements of registration.

Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of H.R. 3381, the Encouraging Public Offerings Act of 2025, sponsored by the chair of the relevant subcommittee, the Capital Markets Subcommittee, that being the gentlewoman from Missouri (Mrs. Wagner).
I urge my colleagues to support this bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: EXPANDING ACCESS TO CAPITAL FOR RURAL JOB CREATORS ACT
statements.title: EXPANDING ACCESS TO CAPITAL FOR RURAL JOB CREATORS ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 1190, the Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act, sponsored by my colleague, the gentleman from Montana (Mr. Downing).
Mr. Speaker, I urge Members to support H.R. 1190, the Expanding Access to Capital for Rural Job Creators Act.
I will point out that I am uniquely unqualified to address this bill since my entire district is in an urban area, that of the great city of Los Angeles.
I strongly support this legislation, which would require the SEC's Office of the Advocate for Small Business Capital Formation to report on capital access issues faced by small, rural businesses.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROMOTING OPPORTUNITIES FOR NON-TRADITIONAL CAPITAL FORMATION ACT
statements.title: PROMOTING OPPORTUNITIES FOR NON-TRADITIONAL CAPITAL FORMATION ACT
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise in strong support of the bill of my good friend and ranking member of the Financial Services Committee (Ms. Waters), which requires the SEC's Office of Small Business Advocate to provide educational resources and host events to promote capital-raising options for small businesses.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HOMEBUYERS PRIVACY PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: HOMEBUYERS PRIVACY PROTECTION ACT
sentences: I thank the sponsors for their good work on this bipartisan bill, and I appreciate that the House is taking action to improve data privacy, in this case with respect to the mortgage market.
Consumer opt-in is an approach that data privacy advocates prefer and one that committee Democrats argued for last Congress when the committee considered former Chair McHenry's version of this bill.
We are not debating consumer privacy in a vacuum.
I wish we were here on the floor preventing Mr. Musk from getting our personal health records, our consumer data, our business records, our Social Security numbers, and our tax data.

After we pass this bill, I hope that the Financial Services Committee would investigate what has happened to consumer protection and what has happened to data privacy, particularly with regard to data obtained from the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and the Treasury Department.

As I have discussed, H.R. 2808 is an important positive step to strengthen data privacy for consumers and curb the harmful practice of trigger leads, protecting consumers from entities that they didn't want to do business with, never sought to do business with, finding out that they are applying for a mortgage and then harassing them with a host of texts and calls, et cetera.
I rise in support of H.R. 2808, the Homebuyers Privacy Protection Act, and I commend Representatives Rose and Torres for introducing it.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: RESCISSIONS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: RESCISSIONS ACT OF 2025
sentences: Mr. Speaker, last month Secretary Rubio responded to me and said no one had died as a result of the gutting of USAID, but Boston University School of Public Health shows us that 300,000 people have died already because they were cut off from food and medicine for tuberculosis, AIDS, and malaria.
The Center for Global Development says that 3.3 million preventable deaths will occur because of the gutting of USAID, but they won't just die there.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: MIRACLE ON ICE CONGRESSIONAL GOLD MEDAL ACT
statements.title: MIRACLE ON ICE CONGRESSIONAL GOLD MEDAL ACT
sentences: I thank the gentleman from Minnesota, and I rise in support of his bill.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISAPPROVING THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF CONSUMER FINANCIAL PROTECTION RELATING TO "DEFINING LARGER PARTICIPANTS OF A MARKET FOR GENERAL-USE DIGITAL CONSUME
statements.title: DISAPPROVING THE RULE SUBMITTED BY THE BUREAU OF CONSUMER FINANCIAL PROTECTION RELATING TO "DEFINING LARGER PARTICIPANTS OF A MARKET FOR GENERAL-USE DIGITAL CONSUMER PAYMENT APPLICATIONS"
sentences: Mr. Speaker, the regulation we are considering now is just a regulation that says that this is an area we are going to look at.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROBLEMS CAUSED BY DOGE CUTS
statements.title: PROBLEMS CAUSED BY DOGE CUTS
sentences: They are doing this in order to justify their plan for a $3.5 trillion tax cut for hedge fund managers, multinational corporations and billionaires, but they are really not saving anything.

Then, yesterday, we passed a budget resolution, and all my Republican colleagues are on Twitter, X, whatever they want to call it, saying that that resolution contains statutory language to say no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security.

They organized the readers content comments to correct falsehoods that people put in their tweets, and every single time a Republican went up and said that that resolution had eliminated taxes on tips, overtime, and Social Security, the Musk organization said: Readers added context.
It does nothing to exempt tips, Social Security, or overtime.
We know they are not ultimately going to do that because they need the $4.5 trillion to provide tax breaks for hedge fund managers, multinational corporations, and billionaires.
They claim that these ads are aimed at undocumented immigrants and that somehow, by watching a 30-second ad, the immigrants are going to say: Oopsy-daisy, I made a mistake.
Venezuela really is better than California.
These are people who walked here from Venezuela.
Whether it is crime in the streets or crime in the suites, we should not defund the police.
We don't defund the men and women in blue, and we don't defund the Securities and Exchange Commission that oversees the stock and bond markets.
It will be because they defunded the police of Wall Street.

Americans are investing in Chinese stocks, and the question I would ask at hearing after hearing is: Can anybody give me a reason why we should use our tax system and lose our tax dollars to incentivize Americans buying Chinese stocks?
We forgo hundreds of millions or billions of dollars in taxes on the gains people earn on investing in Chinese stocks.
Only one Republican has stepped forward and cosponsored my legislation to eliminate the capital gains allowance, the tax incentive for investing in Chinese stocks.
The billionaire class wants subsidies for every investment they make, even when they are building the Chinese economy or the Russian economy or the Iranian economy.
It is time to stand up to the billionaire class.

We also need to take steps so that Chinese stocks are not included in index funds and so that every company that reports to the SEC informs its shareholders of what risk they have due to their dependence on China and what they are doing about it so that every private company is derisking from China and doing everything they can.
We need to tell those who rate the other countries' creditworthiness that if they don't repay a phony debt to China, a debt trap debt to China, that should not be counted against them.
Foreign Aid is a Good Thing Mr. Speaker.
This brings up the issue of foreign aid in general.
If you poll Americans, they will say we are spending too much on foreign aid.
Then you ask them how much of our budget is going to foreign aid.
They say 25 percent of our American budget is going to foreign aid, and it ought to be less.
Then you ask them what percentage should we be spending on foreign aid, and they say 10 percent.
We are spending way less than 1 percent of our budget on foreign aid.
That is why Ronald Reagan recognized the importance of our foreign aid program.
There are some criticisms that are valid against our foreign aid and State Department budget.
We have perfectly good armored cars, but there is a proposal that the State Department spend $400 million on new zero-greenhouse-gas-emitting armored cars.
That money is going to reduce the greenhouse gases of our armored vehicles, and it is going to Elon Musk.
There are a lot of things that are said about our foreign aid budget that are completely false.
Now, why are these foreign aid programs in the interest of America?
If we don't provide foreign aid, China steps in, our influence is declined, and China's influence increases.
I have Republican colleagues who think that USAID is aid that must be food for people who are hungry right now and about to die of starvation.
They don't know that USAID stands for U.S. Agency for International Development.
That is why an Agency for International Development would help Egypt develop its economy.
The people hired in 2024 are those that we are going to need in 2034.

You can also stop all research, and I will get to an example of that, and then you argue, well, hey--in 2026, they can say: Hey, we saved all this money, and the research wouldn't have benefited you by 2026.
You can stop maintenance, and I will get to an example of that.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: DISABLED VETERANS HOUSING SUPPORT ACT
statements.title: DISABLED VETERANS HOUSING SUPPORT ACT
sentences: This deals with the HUD Community Development Block Grant program.
We are dealing with this bill now and about four other bills will go by, and then we will deal with the companion legislation.
Now, we deal with Congresswoman De La Cruz's bill, which I strongly support.
Mr. Speaker, I urge all Members to support both bills.
Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to vote ``yes'' on this bill and its companion legislation.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: HOUSING UNHOUSED DISABLED VETERANS ACT
statements.title: HOUSING UNHOUSED DISABLED VETERANS ACT
sentences: There is nothing more shameful than a homeless, disabled American veteran, one who has lost a limb defending us and now living on the streets.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: ADDRESSING CALIFORNIA WILDFIRES
statements.title: ADDRESSING CALIFORNIA WILDFIRES
sentences: There are those who say that California should not get aid unless we change--get this--our voter registration laws.
Different States have different voter registration processes, and they are all wonderful.
I never once said, no, let's turn to hurricane victims and tell them to keep sleeping on their cousin's couch for months and years until Louisiana changes its abortion laws.
I disagree with Louisiana's abortion laws.
A woman ought to have the right to choose.
He had to tell people that at least he didn't freeze their Social Security checks, although our local health system clinics aren't getting money.

These are the people who are the specialists in toxics removal, dealing with a fire that has caused more Teslas and other electric cars to go up in smoke than any other fire in the history of the world, creating a toxic problem that only a few people know how to deal with.
Our enemies, the terrorists, China, Russia, North Korea and Iran benefit from this.
Finally, it impairs the ability of the CIA to carry on operations that could undercut the support of the Ayatollahs and hopefully bring regime change and democracy to Iran.
The only way to be absolutely sure that you don't have a nuclear Islamic Republic of Iran is not to have an Islamic Republic of Iran.
Another attack that doesn't seem like it is an attack on Americans, but really is, is the decimation of USAID.

Now, I would expect Donald Trump--and I would applaud Donald Trump if he was talking about reforming, reevaluating, reprioritizing USAID, but instead, it seems that he is focused on dismantling USAID.
Just today, Vladimir Putin applauded President Trump for decimating and in effect calling for the abolition of USAID.
Now, Vladimir Putin doesn't care about the Constitution of the United States, but we should.
Under that Constitution, this Congress passed into the law of the land statutes providing for USAID to operate.

First, the Chinese are smart enough not to compliment Donald Trump for destroying USAID because they see an opportunity, particularly in the islands of the Pacific, islands my father risked his life for during World War II.
If you look at the polling, Americans say, well, our foreign aid budget must be 25 percent of our Federal budget, and it should be lower.
Our foreign aid budget is less than 1 percent of our Federal budget.
No one concerned with foreign aid has dreamt of it being 10 percent.
A lot of USAID money is spent to deal with malaria, HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis, Ebola, and bird flu.
Bird flu is combated by USAID around the world, and every chicken that gets bird flu in a very poor country is a chance for that flu to mutate and come to the United States in strength and form.
If you are concerned about the health of Americans and the price we pay for our groceries, USAID's efforts to control disease should matter to you.

Even if you have no morality, even if you do not want to help the least of these with even one quarter of 1 percent of the American GDP, do not take action, Mr. President, that expands the power of the Chinese Communist Party, expands the opportunity for disease around the world, and creates mass migration that will not be stopped by the wall you didn't build.
Then we are told lies about USAID.
He is saying, abolish USAID because of what he did in his first term.
They told the lie that USAID had spent $8 million on subscriptions to POLITICO Pro, a publication.
Yet, the President of the United States first lies and says it was $8 million for USAID and then lies and says, oh, it is some sort of subsidy to some woke, liberal activist publication.
Apparently a U.S. President who doesn't want to spend a dime on USAID wants to build fancy condos for every resident of Gaza.
Second, he has changed the political makeup inside Israel to empower those who believe that the Israeli settlers should move into Gaza and partially displace the Gazan population.

I welcome the recent comments of Israel where they recognize that Hamas fighters are not going to surrender for Israeli prisons and have said that it is acceptable if the Hamas fighters depart the region.
Mr. Speaker, let me focus on one other issue, and that is an issue mentioned by the prior speaker from Arizona: Artificial intelligence.
Trillions of dollars are being spent around the world, more in the United States than anywhere else, to make artificial intelligence more powerful.
